chunks: From him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynan, from Zurara, from Abu al-Khattab who said:

I asked him — meaning Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) — about a man who enters the thicket and finds different eggs therein; he does not know what [bird's] eggs they are — whether eggs of birds that are disliked [to eat] or recommended.

So he [the Imam] said: Therein is a sign that is not hidden. Look at every egg: if you can distinguish its top from its bottom, then eat it; and whatever is equal [i.e. rounded, with both ends the same] in that regard, then leave it.

key_terms.الأجمة: Thicket, reeds, dense vegetation (where wild birds nest)
key_terms.يَسْتَوِي: Is equal/symmetrical (describing eggs with indistinguishable top and bottom — a roundish egg)
key_terms.يُسْتَحَبُّ: Recommended/liked (birds whose meat is halal and preferred)
key_terms.يُكْرَهُ: Disliked/forbidden (in fiqh context, refers to birds whose meat is haram to consume)

ai.seo_question: How can you tell if an unidentified bird egg is halal to eat according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) provides a practical jurisprudential criterion for determining the permissibility of eating unidentified bird eggs found in the wild. The Imam teaches that eggs with a pointed top and a wider bottom — indicating a bird whose meat is permissible — may be eaten, while perfectly symmetrical (round/equal-ended) eggs indicate a forbidden bird and must be avoided. This hadith reflects the Imam's role as the supreme jurisprudential authority for his community, offering a memorable physical test in lieu of species identification.
